relations.definition: Indicates the entity that enforced or levied something.

Fine for favouring booking services -> European Union

chosen_property.label: issuedBy
chosen_property.justification: The property 'issuedBy' aligns with the meaning of an authority granting or providing a formal fine or penalty.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: referee
candidates.comment: A referee relation between a sports event and the person officiating it to enforce rules. Also called officiated by, umpire, judge. Examples: "A football match has a referee 'Pierluigi Collina'.", "A tennis match has a referee 'Eva Asderaki-Moore'.", "A basketball game has a referee 'Joey Crawford'."

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf
candidates.comment: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.

candidates.label: sponsor
candidates.comment: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: legalRepresentative
candidates.comment: A legal representation relation between an organization and the person(s) authorized to act on its behalf in legal matters. Also called authorized representative, legal agent, official representative, corporate officer. Examples: An organization has a legalRepresentative of 'its CEO'. A company's legalRepresentative is 'its sole administrator'. The board appointed 'Jane Doe' as legalRepresentative. Distinct from employee, which is a general employment relation, not specifically legal representation.

candidates.label: constraintProperty
candidates.comment: A definitional relation for a constraint node, indicating a property used as a constraint. Also called "constraining property", "restricted by property", "property constraint". Examples: "Statistical variable constraint node constraintProperty 'schema:age'", "Data filter constraintProperty 'dc:gender'".

candidates.label: legislationLegalForce
candidates.comment: A legal force status relation between a piece of legislation and its current state of being in force. Also called: force status, legal validity, in effect status. Examples: "New Act legislationLegalForce InForce", "Old Regulation legislationLegalForce NotInForce", "Partial Amendment legislationLegalForce PartiallyInForce".

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

relations.definition: Indicates the primary entity that is the focus or recipient of an action or event.

chosen_property.label: recipient
chosen_property.justification: The 'recipient' property captures the idea of an organization being the receiver or focus of a regulatory fine.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: mainEntityOfPage
candidates.comment: A main entity of page relation between a thing and the creative work or URL for which it is the primary described entity. Also called: primary page, described on page, featured on page. Examples: "Albert Einstein mainEntityOfPage Wikipedia Article", "The Election mainEntityOfPage News Report", "Quantum Physics mainEntityOfPage Research Paper". Distinct from mainEntity, which indicates the primary entity described in a creative work.

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: amountOfThisGood

candidates.label: value
candidates.comment: A value relation between a monetary amount, property value, or quantitative value and its specific numerical, textual, boolean, or structured content. candidates.label: requiredQuantity
candidates.comment: A required quantity relation between a how-to item and the amount of that item needed. Also called quantity needed, amount required. Examples: "A how-to item 'sugar' has a required quantity '1 cup'.", "A crafting project needs a required quantity '5 sheets of paper'.", "A recipe step specifies a required quantity '2 eggs'."

candidates.label: referenceQuantity
candidates.comment: A reference quantity relation between a unit price specification and the specific quantity for which the stated price applies. Also called quantity for price, price per quantity. Examples: "A electricity price specification has a reference quantity '4 kWh'.", "A bulk discount has a reference quantity '10 units'.", "A service charge has a reference quantity '1 hour'."

candidates.label: price
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount. Examples: An offer has a price of '19.99'. A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.

candidates.label: orderQuantity
candidates.comment: The number or quantity of a specific item ordered within an order item. Also called item quantity, ordered amount, number of units. Examples: "OrderItem A orderQuantity 2", "OrderItem B orderQuantity 5", "OrderItem C orderQuantity 1". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on total items for shipping.

candidates.label: eligibleQuantity
candidates.comment: An eligible quantity relation between a demand, offer, or price specification and the quantitative value representing the ordering quantities for which it is valid. Also called "valid quantity range", "order quantity limit", "bulk discount quantity". Examples: "Offer 'Bulk Discount' eligibleQuantity 'Minimum 10 units'", "Price specification eligibleQuantity '5-100 items'", "Shipping charge eligibleQuantity 'Over 50 kg'".

candidates.label: doseValue
candidates.comment: A dose value relation between a dose schedule and the number or qualitative value representing the amount of the dose. Also called "dose amount", "quantity per dose". Examples: "Dose schedule doseValue '500'", "Dose schedule doseValue '250'", "Dose schedule doseValue 'High'".

candidates.label: inventoryLevel
candidates.comment: A stock quantity relation between a demand, offer, or product and its current approximate availability in inventory. Also called stock level, quantity in stock, available quantity, current stock. Examples: An offer has an inventoryLevel of '100 units'. A product has an inventoryLevel of 'low stock'. A demand has an inventoryLevel of '50 units available'.

relations.definition: Indicates an alternative name or alias for an entity.

chosen_property.label: equivalentMonetaryValue
chosen_property.definition: Indicates an equivalent monetary value, often in a different currency.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property captures the meaning of an alternative monetary value for a fine, distinct from an alternate name.

candidates.label: alternateName
candidates.comment: An alternate name relation between a thing and an alias or alternative designation for it. Also called alias, alternative designation, other name. Examples: "A city's alternate name is 'The Big Apple'.", "A person's alternate name is 'Liz'."

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

candidates.label: legalName
candidates.comment: An official identification relation between an organization and its formally registered name. Also called registered name, official company name, corporate name, full legal name. Examples: An organization has a legalName of 'Acme Corporation Inc.'. A company's legalName is 'Global Solutions LLC'. The charity's legalName is 'Helping Hands Foundation'. Distinct from name, which is the common or display name.

candidates.label: iupacName
candidates.comment: A chemical nomenclature relation between a molecular entity and its systematic name according to IUPAC recommendations. Also called IUPAC name, systematic chemical name, chemical nomenclature. Examples: A molecular entity has an iupacName of 'sulfuric acid'. A compound has an iupacName of 'ethanol'. A chemical has an iupacName of 'sodium chloride'. Distinct from name, which is a common or trivial name.

candidates.label: sameAs
candidates.comment: A URL that identifies the same real-world entity as the item, providing an unambiguous reference to its identity. Also called equivalent to, identical to, linked identity, canonical URL. Examples: `Person: Albert Einstein` sameAs `Wikipedia URL`, `Organization: Google` sameAs `Official Website URL`, `Product: iPhone` sameAs `Wikidata URL`. Distinct from `url`, which is a general URL for the item, not necessarily an identity link.

candidates.label: additionalName
candidates.comment: An additional name relation between a person and a supplementary name, such as a middle name. Also called middle name, secondary name, other name. Examples: "A person's additional name is 'Marie'.", "John's additional name is 'Fitzgerald'."

candidates.label: alternativeOf
candidates.comment: An alternative of relation between a gene and another gene that represents a variation of it. Also called gene variant, genetic alternative, allele. Examples: "A gene's alternative of is 'Gene B (variant)'.", "Gene A's alternative of is 'Gene A-prime'."

candidates.label: givenName
candidates.comment: A given name relation between a person and their first name. Also called: first name, personal name. Examples: "John Doe" given name "John", "Jane Smith" given name "Jane", "Alice Wonderland" given name "Alice". Distinct from familyName, which is the last name.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: familyName
candidates.comment: A family name relation between a person and their last name. Also called: last name, surname. Examples: "John Doe" family name "Doe", "Jane Smith" family name "Smith", "Alice Wonderland" family name "Wonderland". Distinct from givenName, which is the first name.

relations.definition: Indicates the reason or cause for an event, specifically a recurring action or method.
relations.embedding_query_text: due to practice of: Indicates the reason or cause for an event, specifically a recurring action or method.

chosen_property.label: source
chosen_property.justification: The 'source' property indicates the causal origin of an instantaneous event, which fits the practice causing the fine.

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.

candidates.label: byMonthWeek
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the week(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "week of month", "monthly week recurrence", "on week of month". Examples: "Book club schedule byMonthWeek 2", "Team sync schedule byMonthWeek 1,3".

candidates.label: repeatCount
candidates.comment: A repeat count relation between a schedule and the total number of times a recurring event will occur. Also called number of repetitions, event occurrences. Examples: "A weekly meeting schedule has a repeat count of 10.", "A training course schedule has a repeat count of 5.", "A daily alarm schedule has a repeat count of 365."

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: repeatFrequency
candidates.comment: A repeat frequency relation between a schedule and the interval at which events will recur. Also called recurrence interval, event frequency. Examples: "A meeting schedule has a repeat frequency 'weekly'.", "A workout plan has a repeat frequency 'every other day'.", "A subscription service has a repeat frequency 'monthly'."

candidates.label: actionProcess
candidates.comment: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: qualifiedExpense

candidates.label: acquiredFrom

Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: positiveNotes

Distinct from negativeNotes, which provides negative considerations.

candidates.label: hasTierBenefit
candidates.comment: A tier benefit relation between a member program tier and a specific benefit associated with that tier. Also called tier advantage, member perk, program benefit. Examples: "A loyalty program tier has a tier benefit of free shipping.", "The premium tier has a tier benefit of exclusive access.", "This tier offers a tier benefit of bonus points."

candidates.label: inverseOf

candidates.label: eligibleWithSupplier

Also called "supplier partner", "incentive provider", "valid with retailer". Examples: "Rebate eligibleWithSupplier 'Utility Company X'", "Discount eligibleWithSupplier 'Electronics Store Y'", "Grant eligibleWithSupplier 'Solar Panel Installer Z'".

candidates.label: funding
candidates.comment: A funding relation between a biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product and the grant that provides its direct or indirect financial support. Also called: grant received, sponsorship, financial support. Examples: "Cancer Research Project" funding "NIH Grant R01", "Local Theater Production" funding "Arts Council Grant", "Student Scholarship Program" funding "University Endowment Grant". Distinct from funder, which is the entity providing the funding.

candidates.label: interestRate
candidates.comment: A financial cost/gain relation between a financial product and the percentage rate of interest charged or paid on it. Also called rate of interest, yield, return rate. Examples: A savings account has an interestRate of '0.5%'. A loan has an interestRate of '4.99%'. A bond has an interestRate of '3.2% fixed'. candidates.label: sponsor

candidates.label: about

candidates.label: subjectOf

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview

candidates.label: mentions

candidates.label: appearance

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". candidates.label: claimInterpreter

candidates.label: actionPlatform

candidates.label: object

candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: readBy
candidates.comment: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."

chosen_property.definition: Indicates the concept or quality that the subject is understood or regarded as.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: sameAs
candidates.comment: A URL that identifies the same real-world entity as the item, providing an unambiguous reference to its identity. Also called equivalent to, identical to, linked identity, canonical URL. Examples: `Person: Albert Einstein` sameAs `Wikipedia URL`, `Organization: Google` sameAs `Official Website URL`, `Product: iPhone` sameAs `Wikidata URL`. Distinct from `url`, which is a general URL for the item, not necessarily an identity link.

candidates.label: itemReviewed
candidates.comment: A review subject relation between an aggregate rating or review and the entity that is being evaluated or rated. Also called reviewed item, rated item, subject of review, evaluated entity. Examples: A review has an itemReviewed of 'Restaurant X'. An aggregate rating has an itemReviewed of 'Movie Y'. A product review has an itemReviewed of 'Smartphone Z'. Distinct from itemOffered, which is the subject of an offer or demand.

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

chosen_property.label: perceives
chosen_property.definition: Indicates an action or event that the subject perceives or notices.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property captures the meaning of an organization perceiving an action.

candidates.label: image
candidates.comment: An image relation between any thing and a visual representation of it. Also called picture, photo, visual. Examples: "A product has an image of its front view.", "A person has an image as a profile picture.", "This thing has an image URL."

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: sensoryRequirement
candidates.comment: A description, defined term, or URL detailing the sensory abilities (e.g., hearing, vision) required for a job. Also called sensory abilities, perceptual requirements, job sensory needs. Examples: `Call Center Job` sensoryRequirement `"Excellent hearing"`, `Graphic Designer Role` sensoryRequirement `"Normal color vision"`, `Pilot Position` sensoryRequirement `URL to FAA medical standards`. Distinct from `physicalRequirement`, which is about physical capabilities.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: isSimilarTo
candidates.comment: A functional resemblance relation between two products or services that share similar characteristics or purposes. Also called similar to, comparable to, analogous to, like. Examples: Product A isSimilarTo 'Product B' (a competitor's product). Service X isSimilarTo 'Service Y' (an alternative service). A specific brand of coffee isSimilarTo 'another brand of coffee'. Distinct from isRelatedTo, which is a more general association without implying functional similarity.

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

chosen_property.label: hasConsequenceFor
chosen_property.definition: Indicates an entity that experiences consequences due to the subject.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property captures the meaning of a property having consequences for an organization.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: hasTierRequirement
candidates.comment: A tier requirement relation between a member program tier and a condition for joining that tier. Also called tier eligibility, membership condition, joining requirement. Examples: "A member program tier has a tier requirement of a specific credit card.", "The tier has a tier requirement of a minimum spend.", "This tier requires a tier requirement of an annual fee."
